summary: Feed s106_single is degraded: 7.9% of frames (226/2859, up to 8058 bytes) exceed the IDS 1518-byte MTU and are dropped at the NIC, creating a detection blind spot. Slicing is not viable because the IDS requires full payload.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding jumbo frames (up to 8058 bytes) from jumbo-enabled upstream segments to a 1 Gbps IDS port limited to 1518-byte standard Ethernet MTU. 226 of 2859 frames (7.9%) exceed the limit and are dropped at ingress by the IDS NIC before inspection.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS silently loses 7.9% of traffic. Because it needs full payload for signature and anomaly detection, affected flows are incompletely inspected, causing missed exploits, evasion via large frames, and incomplete forensic evidence.

recommended_fix.why: Tool needs full payload so broker-side slicing/trimming to 1518 bytes would break IDS detection. Fix requires MTU alignment: enable jumbo frame support (>=9000 bytes) on IDS NIC/tool port, or normalize MTU upstream, so large frames are delivered intact without NIC drops.
